Annie Chun is owned by CJ Foods; sauces produced in the U.S.; imported.
UK-owned (AB World Foods); Blue Dragon sauces are produced in the UK, Poland and Thailand. Distribution may involve a Canadian office, but production and sourcing remain overseas.
Crafted at U.S. breweries in California and Georgia, using authentic Japanese fermentation techniques dating back centuries; manufactured stateside and imported, no production in Canada.

Globally headquartered in Japan, with extensive production facilities across the U.S. in states like California, Illinois, Kentucky, Missouri, Tennessee, Michigan, and New York. Although the company creates products for the North American market, none are produced in Canada.
Thai-owned. Produced in factories in Samut Sakhon and Rayong, Thailand. No Canadian manufacturing or ingredients; fully imported

Family-owned company headquartered in Hong Kong. Produced in China, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and the USA. Canadian product often comes from the US (California), sometimes China or elsewhere. No Canadian production or sourcing. Fully imported.
Korean-owned (CJ CheilJedang). Chili pastes produced in South Korea and the USA. No Canadian production or sourcing; all imported.
U.S.-developed and owned (David Tsang; now Hormel Foods). Sauces are produced in the U.S., with no known Canadian manufacturing or sourcing; fully imported.
U.S.-owned (Tran family). Sauces are produced in Irwindale, California. No Canada involvement in production or sourcing. Imported.

Ownership (Company): Lao Gan Ma Special Flavour Foodstuffs Co.
Notes: Chinese-owned (Lao Gan Ma Special Flavour Foodstuffs, founded by Tao Huabi). Manufactured in Guiyang, Guizhou. No Canada involvement. Imported.
Thai-owned (Theppadungporn Coconut Co.). Produced in Thailand (likely central provinces). No Canadian manufacturing or ingredient sourcing; fully imported.
U.S.-based (Chinese-American owners). Chili oils often made in the U.S., typically with imported Sichuan peppers. No Canadian production or sourcing; fully imported to Canada.
Thai-made by various producers. Fully manufactured in Thailand. No Canadian involvement or domestically sourced ingredients; imported.
Thai-owned (Tang Sang Hah Co.). Produced in Thailand. No Canadian manufacturing or sourcing; fully imported.
Thai-owned (Thaitheparos PCL). Produced in Thailand; fully imported with no Canadian production, sourcing, or job creation.
Japanese-made by various regional producers. Fully imported; no Canadian production or ingredient sourcing.
Thai-owned (Theppadungporn Coconut Co.); produced in Thailand. No Canadian production or ingredient sourcing; fully imported.
Thai-owned by Siam Food Products. Crafted in Thailand using premium anchovies and salt with a 2?year fermentation. No Canadian production or sourcing; fully imported.
Traditional Thai-made condiment produced regionally across Thailand. No Canadian production or sourcing; fully imported.
Vietnamese-made (Phu Quoc Island, Kien Giang Province), produced by registered local manufacturers. Protected as a PDO product in the EU and recognized as cultural heritage in V
Vietnamese fish sauce produced in Vietnam. Anchovies sourced near Phu Quoc. U.S.-branded and distributed; fully imported into Canada with no domestic production.
Thai-owned and produced by Thai Fishsauce Factory in Thailand. No Canadian production or ingredient sourcing; fully imported.
Owned by McCormick (U.S.); fish sauce produced in Thailand using traditional anchovy pressing. Fully imported into Canadano domestic manufacturing or sourcing.

U.S.-based (Viet Huong Fish Sauce Co., founded in San Francisco by a China-born immigrant). Fish sauce is fermented in Vietnam or Thailand and blended in Hong Kong, then imported. No Canadian production or sourcing.
Thai-owned (Tang Sang Hah Co.). Manufactured in Thailand using automated production across three factories (Chonburi and Samut Prakan). No Canadian involvement.
U.S.-based (Viet Huong Fish Sauce Co., family-run). Made via fermentation in Vietnam or Thailand, blended in Hong Kong, and imported. No Canadian production or sourcing.
Hong-kong based. Hoisin sauce is produced in its Tai Po facility in Hong Kong, with integrated production and packaging. Fully imported; no Canadian involvement.
Korean-owned (CJ CheilJedang). Doenjang is produced in South Korea, specifically from their Nonsan facility. No Canadian involvement in production or sourcing; fully imported.

Chinese-owned (Sichuan Pixian Douban Co.). Authentic doubanjiang is crafted in Pixian (Chengdu), using traditional fermentation methods and locally sourced ingredients. It holds geographic protection, with no Canadian production or sourcing.
Hong Kong-based (Koon Chun Sauce Factory). Fermented yellow soybean paste is produced in their Yuen Long facility, maintaining traditional fermentation methods. No Canadian production or sourcing.
Hong Kong-owned (Koon Chun Sauce Factory). Hoisin sauce is produced domestically in Yuen Long, Hong Kong. Fully imported; no Canadian involvement.

Hong Kong-based, family-owned company. Hoisin sauce is produced in multiple sites across Hong Kong, China (Xinhui, Huangpu, Jining), the U.S. (Los Angeles), and Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur). No Canadian manufacturing or sourcing.

South Korean-owned (Daesang Corp.). Ssamjang is produced in South Korea under Chung Jung One or O'Food. Daesang has production sites globally (U.S., Poland, China, Vietnam, Indonesia), but no known Canadian operations.
Korean-owned (Daesang Corp.). Chung Jung One soybean pastes are produced in South Korea. No Canadian manufacturing or ingredient sourcing.

Korean-owned (CJ CheilJedang). Haechandle soy-based sauces are produced in South Korea. CJ is expanding globally (plants in Hungary and the U.S.), but no Canadian manufacturing or sourcing currently exists.
Manufactured in China, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and the U.S. Foreign-owned brand headquartered in Hong Kong. No Canadian production, sourcing, or co-packing. Fully imported.
Korean-owned (CJ CheilJedang); sauces produced in Korea and the U.S.; fully imported with no Canadian manufacturing or sourcing.
Filipino-owned (NutriAsia Inc.); manufactured in the Philippines and fully imported into Canada with no local production or sourcing.
Manufactured in the Philippines using locally grown bananas. There is no Canadian production or co-packing, and no known Canadian ingredient sourcing. The product is fully imported.
Manufactured in Japan. These sauces are not produced or co-packed in Canada, nor do they use Canadian ingredients. All product sold in Canada is imported.
Produced in the Philippines, where the sauce is made with locally sourced bananas. There is no evidence of Canadian production, co-packing, or ingredient use. Fully imported.
Produced in South Korea by various Korean manufacturers. There is no Canadian production, no co-packing, and no ingredient sourcing from Canada. The product is fully imported.
Specialty sauce made in Korea; imported.
Filipino brand; sauces produced in the Philippines; imported.
Produced exclusively in Hiroshima, Japan, preserving traditional regional recipes. No evidence of any Canadian manufacturing or ingredient sourcing, fully imported.
Manufactured in the Philippines using locally produced sugarcane. There is no Canadian manufacturing, co-packing, or ingredient use. Fully imported.
Produced in Japan using traditional fermentation methods. No Canadian manufacturing, co-packing, or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
Manufactured in Hong Kong at a facility in Tai Po Industrial Estate. Chinese state-owned via CITIC Group. No manufacturing, co-packing, or ingredient sourcing in Canada. Fully imported.
Produced in Thailand by a Thai-owned company. No Canadian co-packing or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
Manufactured in Samut Sakhon, Thailand. Thai-owned brand. No Canadian involvement in manufacturing or sourcing. Fully imported.
Manufactured in Japan, the USA, and the Netherlands. Japanese-owned. Canadian product generally comes from the U.S., sometimes from Japan. No Canadian manufacturing or co-packing. Imported to Canada.
Manufactured in China, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and the U.S. Foreign-owned brand headquartered in Hong Kong. No Canadian production, sourcing, or co-packing. Fully imported.
Produced in Thailand using traditional methods. Thai-owned. No Canadian co-packing or ingredients. Fully imported.
U.S.-owned and manufactured in the United States. Uses natural ingredients, but no Canadian production or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
Produced in Thailand by a Thai-owned company. No Canadian ingredient sourcing or production. Fully imported.
Manufactured in Hong Kong at a facility in Tai Po Industrial Estate. State-owned via CITIC Group. No Canadian production, co-packing, or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
Brewed in Kentucky using locally grown soybeans and aged in repurposed bourbon barrels. U.S.-owned and manufactured. No Canadian production or co-packing. Fully imported.
Produced in the U.S. using non-GMO soybeans and purified water. American-owned. No production or sourcing in Canada. Fully imported.

Manufacturing (Countries): Korea, USA, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Poland
Notes: Manufactured in multiple countries including Korea, USA, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Poland. South Korean-owned. No Canadian production or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
Manufactured in the Philippines using locally produced ingredients. Filipino-owned. No Canadian co-packing or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
U.S.-owned company. Some products (like traditional shoyu) are brewed in Japan; others are made in the U.S. No Canadian production or co-packing. Fully imported.
Produced in Samut Sakhon, Thailand. Thai-owned. No Canadian manufacturing or sourcing. Fully imported.
Brewed in Japan, the USA, the Netherlands, and Singapore. Japanese-owned. Canadian market often supplied via product made in Wisconsin or California, sometimes from Japan.
Manufactured in Taiwan and imported into Canada. Taiwanese-owned. No Canadian production, ingredient use, or co-packing. Fully imported.

Family-owned company headquartered in Hong Kong. Produced in China, Hong Kong, Malaysia, and the USA. Canadian product often comes from the US (California), sometimes China or elsewhere. No Canadian production or sourcing. Fully imported.

Ownership (Company): Marine Resource Development Co. / Siam Foods
Notes: Brewed in Thailand using traditional methods. Thai-owned. No co-packing or ingredient sourcing in Canada. Fully imported.
U.S.-owned company. Most seaweed-based sauces are produced in California; some sources claim Chinese manufacturing. No Canadian production or co-packing. Fully imported.

Chinese state-owned producer. Primary soy sauce manufacturing occurs in Guangdong, China. Some products (e.g., U.S. market) may be bottled or processed in the U.S. No Canadian production or sourcing. Fully imported.

U.S. subsidiary of a Japanese company. Tamari is brewed in Henrico, Virginia, USA. No manufacturing or co-packing in Canada. They say they "try" to use soy beans from US or Canada "when possible" - vague. Fully imported.
South Korean-owned brand; soy sauce production occurs in the Philippines for export. No Canadian production or ingredient sourcing. Fully imported.
Filipino-owned brand. While some bottles are labelled as imported by Canadian distributors, actual production remains in the Philippines. No known Canadian co-packing.
Japanese-owned company. Production based in Japan and Oregon (USA). No facilities or co-packing arrangements in Canada. Fully imported.
After 73 years, Lee's Food Products closed its Leslieville, Toronto factory. Apparently China Lily soy is still available on store shelves.
Loblaw's private label. The bottle indicates "Prepared in Canada"; we have not yet confirmed who the 3rd-party contractor is, however.
Sobey's private label. The bottle indicates "Prepared in Canada"; we have not yet confirmed who the 3rd-party contractor is, however.
Metro's private label. The bottle indicates "Prepared in Canada"; we have not yet confirmed who the 3rd-party contractor is, however.
Confirmed made in Canada; very little other information exists on the brand.
100% Canadian-owned (Victoria, BC). Produces single malts using Vancouver Island water and Canadian malted barley. All distilling, aging, and bottling in BC.
Independent Canadian ownership (Nova Scotia). Pioneer of Canadian single malt (Glen Breton). Uses Canadian barley and spring water from Cape Breton. Distilled, matured, and bottled on site.
Family-owned in British Columbia. Grain-to-glass distillery using 100% BC-grown grains. All whisky production in Vernon and Kelowna, BC.
Independent, family-owned (Alberta). Produces whisky in High River, AB. Uses Canadian prairie grains. Distilling, aging, and bottling all in Alberta.
Family-run, organic craft distillery (BC). Known for organic single malt whisky. Uses Canadian organic barley. All production in Pemberton, BC.
Independent, Yukon-based. Produces small-batch single malt whiskies. Uses Canadian grains (sourced from prairies & Yukon where possible). Fully made and aged in Whitehorse.
Family-owned, Vancouver Island. Produces single malt whisky using locally grown barley and BC water. All distilling and maturation on site.
Independent Saskatchewan distillery. Grain-to-glass operation using 100% Saskatchewan-grown rye, corn, and barley. Whisky distilled, matured, and bottled on site.
Vancouver craft distillery, Canadian-owned. Produces whisky alongside gin/vodka. Uses local BC grain. All whisky made and matured in Vancouver.
Ontario craft distillery, Canadian-owned. Uses Ontario grain. Produces small-batch whisky alongside gin/liqueurs. Fully made in Stratford, ON.
Revelstoke, BC craft distillery, Canadian-owned. Uses Canadian malted barley and other local grains. Produces whisky on site.
Independent BC distillery. Canadian-owned. Uses Canadian grains (focus on rye and corn). Distillation and aging in Delta, BC.
Ontario, Canadian-owned. Produces whisky alongside gin, bitters, etc. Uses Ontario grain. All whisky distilled and aged locally.
Quebec artisanal distillery, family-owned. Uses Quebec grains. Produces small-batch whisky. Entire process in Petit-Paquetville, NB (with Quebec facilities also).
Quebec craft distillery, Canadian-owned. Uses local Quebec grain. Whisky distilled and matured in Gatineau, QC.
BC-owned. Uses local BC grain for whisky production. Produces other spirits too. Made in Nanaimo, BC.
Independent Calgary distillery. Canadian-owned. Uses Alberta grain. Produces whisky, brandy, and other spirits.
Farm-to-glass, independent Alberta distillery. Uses locally grown Alberta barley and rye. All whisky production on site.
Nova Scotia, Canadian-owned. Uses local Nova Scotia grain and molasses. Produces whisky alongside rum, gin, etc.
Saskatchewan family-owned. Uses local Saskatchewan grain. Produces whisky and other spirits in Lumsden, SK.
New Brunswick, Canadian-owned. Produces craft whisky with locally grown grains. Distilled and matured on site.
Quebec artisanal distillery, Canadian-owned. Produces single malts and rye whiskies with local Quebec grain. All production in Quebec.
BC distillery, Canadian-owned. Produces single malt whisky with BC-sourced barley. Made in Oliver, BC.
Surrey, BC, Canadian-owned. Maker of Lohin McKinnon whisky. Uses Canadian malted barley. All whisky distilled and aged in BC.
Vancouver Island, Canadian-owned. Maker of Glen Saanich single malt whisky. Uses BC-grown barley. Entirely island-based production.
Calgary, Canadian-owned. Produces whisky alongside gin and vodka. Uses Alberta grain. Made and aged in Alberta.
Vancouver Island, Canadian-owned. Produces whisky using BC grains and ocean-side aging conditions. Also famous for gin.
Gibsons, BC craft distillery. Canadian-owned. Produces small-batch whisky using local grains.
South Surrey, BC, Canadian-owned. Produces whisky from local BC grains. Small-batch Canadian whisky house.
Salt Spring Island, BC, Canadian-owned. Produces whisky along with gin/liqueurs. Uses local BC grains. Entire production on island.
Owned by Pernod Ricard (via Corby Spirit & Wine, France/Canada). Produced in Windsor, Ontario. Made from 100% locally grown rye, distilled in copper pot stills, and aged in new oak casks.
Owned by Pernod Ricard (via Corby Spirit & Wine). Produced in Windsor, Ontario. Uses Canadian-grown grains, with aging in barrels sourced internationally (often rum or sherry casks).
Owned by Pernod Ricard (via Corby Spirit & Wine). Historic Toronto brand revived in Ontario. Produced in Windsor using Canadian corn, rye, and barley. Distilled, aged, and bottled in Canada.

Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan). Made in Calgary, Alberta. Uses 100% Canadian-grown rye grain (main marketing claim). Fermentation, distillation, and aging all in Alberta. Strongest case for full Canadian sourcing among big brands.

Owned by Sazerac (USA). Produced in Collingwood, Ontario. Uses Canadian grain (corn, rye, barley), but as with most majors, sourcing is mostly Canadian, not guaranteed 100%. Manufactured fully in Ontario.
Owned by Sazerac (USA). Produced in Canada (exact facilities vary). Uses Canadian-style blends of rye, corn, barley. Primarily Canadian grains, but sourcing specifics not transparent.

Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan). Produced in Windsor, Ontario. Historically used Ontario & prairie grains, today still mostly Canadian but may include imported grain through Suntory’s supply chains. Matured and bottled in Canada.
Owned by Campari Group (Italy). Distilled in Grimsby, Ontario. Uses corn, rye, and barley, primarily Canadian-grown. Manufacturing, blending, and aging are all in Ontario.
Owned by Pernod Ricard (France), operated by Corby Spirit & Wine (Canada). Produced in Windsor, Ontario. Uses corn, rye, and barley, mostly Canadian-sourced, but some foreign rye may be blended.
Owned by Heaven Hill Brands (USA). Produced in Lethbridge, Alberta. Grain bill of corn, rye, barley, mostly Canadian prairie-sourced. Distillation, maturation, and bottling are all in Canada.

Owned by William Grant & Sons (Scotland). Produced in Ontario (Windsor, under Wiser’s/Corby facilities). Uses a typical Canadian grain blend (corn, rye, barley), primarily Canadian-sourced, but not exclusively. Aged and bottled in Canada.

Owned by Sazerac (USA). Produced in Manitoba and Ontario (depending on batching). Originally Seagram’s (Canadian family brand). Now grain sourcing is mostly Canadian, with potential foreign supplementation.
Owned by Diageo (UK). Manufactured in Gimli, Manitoba. Uses corn, rye, and barley. Corn & barley largely Canadian, but rye often imported from the U.S.. Fully produced and aged in Canada.
Owned by Diageo (UK). Produced in Scotland as a blended Scotch using malt and grain whiskies from many Diageo distilleries. All manufacturing and aging in Scotland, grains primarily UK-sourced.
Owned by Pernod Ricard (France). Produced in Scotland. A blended Scotch whisky using malt from Strathisla and other distilleries. Grain and malt sourcing is primarily Scottish.
Owned by William Grant & Sons (Scotland). Produced in Dufftown, Speyside. One of the largest single malt distilleries. Uses Scottish barley and pure Speyside water.
Owned by Pernod Ricard (France). Produced in Speyside, Scotland. Single malt whisky using Scottish barley and spring water.
Owned by Edrington Group (Scotland). Produced in Craigellachie, Speyside. Premium single malt aged in sherry casks, made from Scottish barley and Highland spring water.
Owned by Diageo (UK). Produced on Islay, Scotland. Famous for heavily peated single malt. Uses Scottish barley, malted with peat smoke.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan). Produced on Islay, Scotland. Heavily peated single malt made with local Islay water and Scottish barley.
Owned by Diageo (UK). Produced in Oban, West Highlands. Single malt made with Scottish barley and spring water.
Owned by Diageo (UK). Produced on the Isle of Skye, Scotland. Known for maritime character. Single malt made with Scottish barley.
Owned by LVMH/Moët Hennessy (France). Produced on Islay, Scotland. Heavily peated single malt made with Scottish barley and Islay water.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan). Produced on Islay, Scotland. One of Scotland’s oldest licensed distilleries. Uses Scottish barley, some floor-malted onsite.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan). Produced near Glasgow, Lowlands. Known for triple distillation. Uses Scottish barley.
Owned by William Grant & Sons (Scotland). Produced in Dufftown, Speyside. Single malt made with Scottish barley, featuring traditional floor maltings and in-house cooperage.
Owned by LVMH/Moët Hennessy (France). Produced in Tain, Highland. Single malt made with Scottish barley and tallest stills in Scotland.
Owned by Whyte & Mackay (Emperador Inc., Philippines). Produced in Alness, Highlands. Premium single malt matured in sherry casks. Made from Scottish barley and Highland water.
Owned by Edrington Group (Scotland). Produced in Orkney. Single malt known for balanced peat. Uses Scottish barley and Orkney spring water.
Owned by Pernod Ricard (France). Produced in Speyside. Single malt matured in sherry and bourbon casks. Made with Scottish barley.
Owned by Brown-Forman (USA). Produced in Speyside. Offers both peated and unpeated styles. Uses Scottish barley and water.
Owned by Brown-Forman (USA). Produced in Highlands (Forgue). Known for sherry-cask matured single malts. Uses Scottish barley.
Independent, Irish-owned. Produced in Dublin. Makes Irish whisky (single malt, pot still, blends) using Irish-grown grains.
Produced by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard) under license for Mitchell & Son. Single pot still whisky made at Midleton Distillery using Irish barley.
Produced by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard) for Mitchell & Son. Single pot still whisky aged in multiple casks. Made with Irish barley.
Owned by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard). Produced at Midleton, Ireland. Classic Irish whisky, single pot still style, made with Irish barley.
Owned by Walsh whisky (Irish independent). Produced in Ireland (contract-distilled at Midleton). Blended Irish whisky, pot still and malt, using Irish barley.
Owned by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard). Produced at Midleton, Ireland. Best-selling Irish whisky worldwide. Blend of pot still and grain whiskys made with Irish barley.
Owned by Proximo Spirits (USA). Produced in Northern Ireland. Single malt and blends made with Irish barley and water from the River Bush.
Owned by William Grant & Sons (Scotland). Produced in Tullamore, Ireland. Triple-distilled blended Irish whisky made from Irish-grown barley.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan/USA). Produced in Clermont, Kentucky. Uses primarily Kentucky-grown corn with rye and malted barley (U.S. sourced). Largest bourbon brand worldwide.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan/USA). Distilled in Loretto, Kentucky. Famous wheated bourbon (corn, wheat, malted barley) all U.S.-sourced grains. Fully produced and aged in Kentucky.
Owned by Sazerac (USA). Distilled in Frankfort, Kentucky. Uses U.S.-grown corn, rye, barley. Flagship bourbon, with multiple mashbills.
Owned by Brown-Forman (USA). Distilled in Versailles, Kentucky. Premium bourbon brand. Uses U.S.-grown corn, rye, barley.
Owned by Campari Group (Italy/USA). Distilled in Lawrenceburg, Kentucky. Uses U.S. grains (corn, rye, barley). Classic bourbon brand.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan/USA). Produced in Clermont, Kentucky. Traditional bourbon mashbill with U.S. corn, rye, and barley. Fully aged in Kentucky.
Owned by Diageo (UK/USA). Produced in Kentucky (sourced distilling, much from Four Roses historically, now Bulleit Distillery in Shelbyville). Uses high-rye mashbill with U.S. corn and rye.
Owned by Kirin Brewery (Japan/USA). Distilled in Lawrenceburg, Kentucky. All U.S.-grown corn, rye, and malted barley. Known for multiple mashbills and yeast strains.
Owned by Heaven Hill (USA). Distilled in Bardstown, Kentucky. Uses U.S.-grown corn, rye, and barley. Straight bourbon.
Owned by Heaven Hill (USA). Kentucky bourbon, produced in Louisville/Bardstown. Grain sourcing entirely U.S. (corn, rye, barley).
Owned by Brown-Forman (USA). Produced in Louisville, Kentucky. One of the oldest bourbon brands. Uses U.S. corn, rye, barley.
Owned by Campari Group (Italy/USA). Produced at Wild Turkey Distillery, Kentucky. Uses U.S.-grown corn, rye, and barley. Premium small-batch bourbon.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan/USA). Small-batch bourbon brand, produced in Kentucky with U.S. grain sourcing. Limited releases.
Owned by Beam Suntory (Japan/USA). Distilled in Kentucky, using corn, rye, and barley. All U.S.-grown. Small-batch bourbon.
Owned by Brown-Forman (USA). Produced in Lynchburg, Tennessee. Tennessee whisky (similar to bourbon, filtered through maple charcoal). Uses Tennessee/US corn, rye, barley.
Owned by Diageo (UK/USA). Produced in Cascade Hollow, Tennessee. Tennessee whisky using U.S. grains.

Owned by Suntory (Japan). Produced entirely in Japan. A blended whisky combining malt whiskies from Yamazaki and Hakushu and grain whisky from Chita. Aged in multiple cask types including American oak, sherry, and Mizunara Japanese oak.

Owned by Suntory (Japan). Japan’s first malt whisky distillery, founded in 1923. Produces single malt whisky using Japanese water, aged in American, Spanish, and Mizunara oak casks. Barley is mostly imported from Scotland.

Owned by Suntory (Japan). Distilled in Yamanashi Prefecture since 1973. Produces single malt whisky, with unpeated and peated styles. Barley imported, but distillation, maturation, and blending are fully Japanese.
Owned by Asahi Group (Japan). Produces whisky at Yoichi and Miyagikyo distilleries. Uses Japanese water and mostly imported malted barley. Fully distilled and aged in Japan.
Owned by King Car/TTL (Taiwan). Produced in Yilan County, Taiwan. Uses both local water and imported barley. Fully distilled and aged in Taiwan’s hot, humid climate.
Owned by Amrut Distilleries (India). Produced in Bangalore. Uses Indian barley (from Punjab and Rajasthan) and local water. A pioneer of Indian single malt.
Owned by John Distilleries (India). Produced in Goa. Uses Indian six-row barley and local water. Fully Indian-made single malts.
Owned by Irish Distillers (Pernod Ricard). Produced at Midleton, Ireland. Single pot still whisky, 100% Irish barley.

Independent, owned by Venture Whisky Ltd. (Japan). Founded in 2008 by Ichiro Akuto. Produces single malt whiskies using local Japanese water, Mizunara oak washbacks, and some imported barley. Operates its own cooperage and floor maltings.
Owned by Hombo Shuzo (Japan). Distilled at the Shinshu Mars Distillery in Nagano, Japan’s highest-altitude whisky site. Fully Japanese-owned and produced, with domestic ingredients where possible.
Owned by Kirin (Japan). Produced at the Fuji Gotemba Distillery near Mount Fuji. Fully Japanese ownership and manufacturing. Grains are partly imported but all distilling and aging are in Japan.

Owned by New World Whisky Distillery (Australia), with minority investment from Diageo. Produced in Melbourne. Uses Australian barley and local casks, especially wine barrels. Entirely Australian production.
Owned by Lark Distilling Co. (Australia). Produces single malt whisky in Tasmania using locally sourced barley and water. Fully Australian-owned and produced.
Independent Tasmanian distillery. Produces award-winning single malt whisky. Uses Tasmanian barley and pure local water. 100% Australian-made.

Canadian family-owned company with all production in Canada. These car wash strips are biodegradable and made using local labor and packaging. Nature Clean’s long-standing eco credentials and in-country operations make it highly Canadian.

Product Name: Eco Living Club Dishwasher Detergent Strips
Notes: Made in Canada with eco-friendly, septic-safe formulations. The company’s focus is on sustainable packaging and local employment. Fully Canadian-owned with no overseas production.
Myni’s dishwasher tablets are manufactured in Canada using plant- and mineral-based ingredients. They are plastic-free, and the company is entirely Canadian-owned and operated.

Product Name: Buck Naked Soap Company Shampoo Bar
Notes: A Canadian-owned company based in Ontario. All products are handcrafted in small batches in Canada using ethically sourced, plant-based ingredients. No foreign manufacturing. A strong local employment and ingredient sourcing focus.
